extraction.name: Fast Training Methods for CIFAR-10
extraction.description: This paper introduces training methods for the CIFAR-10 dataset that achieve high accuracy (94%, 95%, 96%) in significantly reduced time (3.29s, 10.4s, 46.3s respectively) on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. It proposes a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation called 'alternating flip' to improve training speed and efficiency.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.citeAs: Jordan, K. (2024). 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU. arXiv preprint arXiv:2404.00498v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset used is CIFAR-10, which is a pre-existing dataset containing 60,000 32x32 color images labeled into ten classes. The paper does not collect new data but utilizes the existing CIFAR-10 training set (50,000 images) and test set (10,000 images).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 dataset, which contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. Divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper describes data manipulation through augmentation techniques, specifically 'alternating flip' (a derandomized horizontal flipping augmentation) and random translation. It also mentions using reflection padding for translation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data is loaded using a custom GPU-accelerated dataloader. Images are normalized using CIFAR mean and standard deviation. For training, random horizontal flipping (alternating or random) and 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding are applied. For evaluation, test-time augmentation (TTA) is used, involving horizontal flipping and cropping.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The labels for the CIFAR-10 dataset are pre-existing and were created by human annotators (as part of the original CIFAR-10 dataset creation). The paper does not perform new annotation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to accelerate research and reduce the cost of experiments by speeding up training. This allows researchers to iterate faster and conduct studies requiring massive numbers of trained networks with fewer computational resources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The methods are optimized for training speed on CIFAR-10 with fixed hardware constraints (single NVIDIA A100). The performance gains are specific to the algorithmic improvements and may not generalize directly to other datasets without tuning, although some generalization to CIFAR-100, SVHN, and CINIC-10 is demonstrated. The compiled version requires a one-time compilation cost, making it less suitable for single runs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training neural networks on CIFAR-10 for research purposes, specifically to accelerate experimental iteration and reduce computational costs. It is intended for scenarios where many networks are trained at once or where rapid hyperparameter comparison is needed.
